method.label: Unfold the faces and compare areas

annotationRationale: Congruent-face edge correspondences and parallelogram diagonals support the folding argument. The cosine law identifies acute faces, while Heron's formula computes the candidate area and supplies a bound excluding every other integer triple.
sourceMethod: Followed the official parallelogram-hinge argument and its Heron-formula evaluation for sides 4, 5, 6. Added details establishing foldability and a Heron-based comparison to justify the official minimum claim over all integer triples.

review.mathCheck: The opposite-edge labeling and hinge argument correctly establish acuteness; the continuous folding construction proves existence without including flat endpoints. Integer acuteness forces a≥4 and b≥5. The face (4,5,6) gives total area \(15\sqrt7\). Every other eligible triple has b≥6 and \((4K)^2>3a^2b^2\ge1728>1575\), proving the global minimum, choice D.
review.sourceMethodCheck: Faithful, originally worded adaptation of MAA #24, pages 16-17, including the parallelogram hinge figure and Heron approach. The added existence argument and area bound correctly justify steps abbreviated in the official solution. The labeled construction is reconstructible without an additional figure.
review.annotationCheck: All five selected nodes are relevant, with the three assessed skills and two geometric supporting skills correctly distinguished.
